paragraphs.en: In Baghdad during al-Mustansir Billah's reign, the caliph favored the poor and learned. One day, he was angered by ten men and ordered their arrest on a feast day.
paragraphs.zh: 在阿尤布·比拉勒统治下的巴格达，哈里发偏爱贫穷而有学问的人。一天，他因十个人的行为而愤怒，在节日当天下令逮捕他们。

paragraphs.en: That night, Shahrazad paused her tale. Dinarzad urged, "Sister, what an amazing story!" Shahrazad replied, "Wait until tomorrow; I have more to tell if you are spared."
paragraphs.zh: 那天晚上，沙赫拉兹暂停了她的讲述。丁扎兹急切地说：“姐姐，这个故事真是太精彩了！”沙赫拉兹答道：“等明天吧；如果你能保住性命，我还有很多精彩的故事要讲。”

paragraphs.en: On the following night, Shahrazad began:
paragraphs.zh: 在接下来的那个夜晚，沙海雅德开始了她的讲述：

paragraphs.en: O King, I heard that the tailor told the king of China that the barber said to his guests:
paragraphs.zh: 国王陛下，裁缝曾对中国的国王说，理发师在对他的客人说道：

paragraphs.en: The caliph ordered the police chief of Baghdad to bring ten robbers to a feast for execution. The chief captured them and took them on a boat. Seeing this, I secretly joined them out of a sense of camaraderie.
paragraphs.zh: 哈里发命令巴格达的警察局长抓十名强盗带到宴会上处决。局长捕获了他们，并将他们带上了船。看到这一幕，出于一种同仇敌忾的感觉，我也悄悄加入了他们的行列。

paragraphs.en: We crossed the river, and upon reaching Baghdad, we were chained by guards. Despite my silence, they were beheaded one by one until only I remained.
paragraphs.zh: 我们渡过了河，抵达巴格达后，被守卫用锁链锁了起来。尽管我一言不发，他们一个个都被斩首，直到只剩下我一人。

paragraphs.en: The caliph noticed me and asked why I stayed silent. He then pointed out that there should have been ten heads. The executioner insisted he had beheaded all ten.
paragraphs.zh: 哈里发注意到我，问我为何沉默不语。他接着指出应该有十颗头才对。行刑人坚持说自己已经砍下了全部十颗头。

paragraphs.en: Upon counting, it was confirmed that nine heads were present. The caliph questioned my silence and my association with the robbers, noting my advanced age but lack of understanding.
paragraphs.zh: 经过清点，的确有九个脑袋。哈里发注意到我沉默不语，并且与强盗有所牵连，他虽然留意到我的年迈，却也察觉出我不甚明白其中缘由。

paragraphs.en: I explained, "O Commander of the Faithful, I am the Silent One. My wisdom and eloquence are unparalleled. I joined these men believing they were going to have a party.
paragraphs.zh: 我解释说：“尊贵的哈里发陛下，我是沉默者。我的智慧与口才无出其右。我加入他们时以为他们会举办一场聚会。”

paragraphs.en: Now, despite my kindness, I face this fate."
paragraphs.zh: 尽管我善待了他，如今仍落得如此境地。

paragraphs.en: The caliph laughed when I spoke, realizing my true nature: generous and reticent, unlike the young man who had wronged me after I saved him. He asked if my six brothers were like me. I replied that they were each afflicted with a bodily defect—blind, one-eyed, hunchbacked, paraplegic, ear-cropped, or lip-cropped.
paragraphs.zh: 当我开口说话时，哈里发听后笑了起来，他意识到我的真实本性：慷慨而寡言，与那个在我救了他的命之后还对我施以不义的年轻人截然不同。他问我六个兄弟是否也像我一样。我回答说，他们每个人都有身体上的缺陷——一个是瞎子，一个独眼，一个驼背，一个下肢瘫痪者，还有一个耳朵被割过，另一个则是嘴唇被割过的。

paragraphs.en: I emphasized that despite their tales, I was more valuable and spoke less than them.
paragraphs.zh: 我强调尽管他们有很多故事要讲，但我更加宝贵，而且说话却不多。

paragraphs.en: The eldest brother, the tailor, began his story, but Shahrazad was interrupted by dawn's light.
paragraphs.zh: 大哥哥裁缝开始讲述他的故事，但苏赫拉布被黎明的曙光打断了。
第二天晚上，沙海拉扎德接着说：

paragraphs.en: O happy king, the tailor recounted his tale to the Chinese king, who in turn heard it from the barber.
paragraphs.zh: 快乐的国王啊，裁缝将他的故事讲述给了中国国王，而国王又是从理发师那里听来的。
